literal: Shaving [the head] and growing [the hair] long are not required, if [one] completely avoids that which the world condemns.
translation: There is no need for shaving the head or growing the hair long, if one completely avoids those actions that the world condemns.
modern: உலகம் பழிக்கும் செயல்களைத் தவிர்த்துவிட்டால், தலையை மழிப்பதோ அல்லது முடியை வளர்ப்பதோ தேவையில்லை.
explanation: This couplet concludes the chapter on inconsistent conduct by highlighting that external symbols of asceticism are meaningless without inner discipline. The poet states that shaving one's head or growing one's hair long—common outward signs of renunciation—are entirely unnecessary. What truly matters is the internal restraint to avoid actions that are condemned by wise people in the world. True renunciation lies in the purity of conduct, not in external appearances.
